title: Deeper and broader peer-validation methodology and evidence-cost refresh
mode: primary-source web research and read-only local plan/test-owner inspection
scope: Compare test, fuzz, timeout, and diagnostic practices in LibreDWG, ezdxf, and ACadSharp
Map peer test practices to the existing fast local, scheduled hardening, optional peer, and native-consumer lanes
Refine implementation readiness without increasing per-slice validation cost or adding peer fixtures

method.kind: Read current upstream project documentation/source and inspect local plan and CMake test ownership
method.limitations: Upstream master documentation and source are mutable and describe project practices, not a pinned peer execution or conformance result. No peer corpus was downloaded or copied. Research refines validation lanes only; the local CTest crash recorded in the plan remains unattributed and is not resolved by this pass.

sources.revision: mutable master docs and repository inventory reviewed 2026-10-18
sources.observed: The project exposes separate DXF checks, serial/parallel logging scripts, timeout guidance for large or hanging DWG inputs, dwgfuzz/LLVM fuzz frontends, and a separate fuzz setup. These define useful bounded validation lanes but do not establish any peer corpus result as libdxfrw conformance.

The documented test command covers separate tests and integration_tests. Documentation describes optional compiled C extensions and a source path that can run without them, so optional runtime profile is part of reproducibility.

sources.revision: mutable master docs/examples and maintainer response reviewed 2026-10-18
sources.observed: Reader examples subscribe to OnNotification for warnings/information. The maintainer says the samples directory is used by the project test suite. A successful Read() without diagnostics and per-object dispositions is incomplete peer evidence; peer samples are not locally authored test fixtures.

sources.revision: working tree over baseline de27a3391a624aba03ca71f3583c4b3a6e6396a9 reviewed 2026-10-18
sources.observed: Existing plan and CMake target ownership already separate generated focused tests, owning CTest, compatibility builds, full-suite checkpoints, and optional peer/native evidence. This research consolidates the peer practices into those lanes; it does not require a new test owner or recurring external execution.

assessment.planImpact: Clarifies that each local slice uses the existing strict touched target, focused generated selector, relevant compatibility target, and owning CTest; peer differential, stress/fuzz, and native checks remain scheduled/composed and diagnostic-rich. Missing external evidence is non-blocking for independent local work.

implementationReadyChecks: Continue the dependency-ready local queue without waiting for a peer build or remote corpus.
Use a generated local control and existing test owner for each changed path; add no peer/customer DWG/DXF fixture.
Per-slice validation remains strict touched target, focused selector, relevant compatibility target, and owning CTest.
At an optional peer checkpoint, pin artifact/runtime/profile and capture warnings, errors, recovery actions, and every source identity disposition.
Run large-corpus, fuzz, sanitizer, peer-matrix, and native platform checks only at the existing scheduled/composed gates, with bounded resources.
After each committed implementation slice, update status and next action and report progress; record unavailable external gates as non-blocking statuses.
